extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (computational number theorists, mathematicians and programmers using PARI/GP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions: preconditions, behaviour, flags, outputs and implementation notes for number-theoretic, polynomial, series and linear-algebra routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolred(nf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative version of polred: given a monic polynomial pol with coefficients in nf, finds a list of relative polynomials defining some subfields, hopefully simpler and containing the original field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In version 2.0.19 slower than rnfpolredabs. Library syntax: rnfpolred(nf, pol, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolredabs(nf, pol, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative version of polredabs: given a monic polynomial pol with coefficients in nf, finds a simpler relative polynomial defining the same field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 returns [P,a] where a is an element whose characteristic poly is pol; if flag=2 returns an absolute polynomial. Faster and more efficient than rnfpolred in current implementation. Library syntax: rnfpolredabs(nf, pol, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpseudobasis(nf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given number field nf (from nfinit) and polynomial pol defining a relative extension L of nf, computes a pseudo-basis (A,I) and the relative discriminant of L; output [A,I,D,d].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D is the relative ideal discriminant, d is relative discriminant in nf*/nf*^2. nf may be a bnf from bnfinit. Library syntax: rnfpseudobasis(nf, pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfsteinitz(nf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a pseudo-basis (A,I) (not necessarily HNF) for a relative extension L of nf so that all ideals of I except maybe the last are equal to the ring of integers of nf; outputs [A,I,D,d].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input x may be a defining polynomial or a pseudo-basis (e.g., from rnfpseudobasis). The last ideal's class is the Steinitz class. nf may be a bnf. Library syntax: rnfsteinitz(nf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: subgrouplist(bnr,{bound},{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnr (from bnrinit) or a list of cyclic components of a finite Abelian group G, output the list of subgroups of G (optionally bounded by index 'bound').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroups are given as HNF left divisors of the SNF matrix. If flag=0 and bnr is from bnrinit, only subgroups whose modulus is the conductor are given. Library syntax: subgrouplist0(bnr,bound,flag,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: zetak(znf, x, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the Dedekind zeta function of the number field (znf from zetakinit) at complex number x; if flag=1 compute Dedekind Lambda function instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy depends critically on zetakinit initialization and current precision; results may be off by up to 5–10 decimal digits. Library syntax: glambdak(znf,x,prec) or gzetak(znf,x,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: zetakinit(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute initialization data for a number field defined by polynomial x necessary to compute Dedekind zeta and lambda functions; calls bnfinit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is a 9-component vector of technical data; only v[1][4] (bnfinit result) is generally usable directly. Very inefficient; may need millions of Dirichlet series coefficients for high precision and large discriminants (practical limits ~9 digits relative precision for non-small discriminants). Library syntax: initzeta(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: O(a^b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation for p-adic (if a integer >=2) or power-series zero otherwise, with precision given by b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ggrandocp(a,b) where b is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: deriv(x,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivative of x with respect to main variable or v; scalar derivative is zero, vectors/matrices componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x cannot be polmod. Shortcut x' can indicate derivative wrt main variable. Library syntax: deriv(x,v) with omitted v coded as -1.

rubrics_metrics.name: eval(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace formal variables in x by their assigned values (GP-mode evaluation), not substitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in GP interactive mode. Applying eval to a string runs the corresponding GP command. Library syntax: geval(x). For polynomials use poleval, qf_eval, hqf_eval for specific types.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorpadic(pol,p,r,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: p-adic factorization of polynomial pol to precision r; result is two-column matrix like factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: r must be strictly larger than p-adic valuation of discriminant. Default method: modified round 4 (Zassenhaus). If flag=1 use Buchmann–Lenstra algorithm (usually less efficient). Library syntax: factorpadic4(pol,p,r) with r long.

rubrics_metrics.name: intformal(x,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal integration of x with respect to main variable or v; logarithmic terms may cause errors because PARI evaluates abstract logs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x may be any type; rational function base ring assumed integral domain char 0. Library syntax: integ(x,v) with omitted v coded as -1.

rubrics_metrics.name: padicappr(pol,a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of p-adic roots of pol congruent to p-adic number a modulo p (or 4 if p=2) with same p-adic precision as a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a can be a t_PADIC or element of finite extension (t_POLMOD); if latter, result roots belong to same extension. Library syntax: apprgen9(pol,a) (or apprgen(pol,a) when a is t_PADIC).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcoeff(x,s,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Coefficient of degree s of polynomial x with respect to main variable or v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: polcoeff0(x,s,v) with omitted v coded -1. Also available: truecoeff(x,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldegree(x,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of polynomial or rational function x in main variable or v; conventions: degree(0) = -1; non-zero scalar degree 0; errors otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: poldegree(x,v) with omitted v coded -1. degree(x) equals poldegree(x,-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcyclo(n,{v=x})
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th cyclotomic polynomial in variable v (default x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n must be positive. Library syntax: cyclo(n,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldisc(pol,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of polynomial pol in main variable or v; algorithm: subresultant algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: poldisc0(x,v). Alternative discsr(x) equivalent to poldisc0(x,-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldiscreduced(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced discriminant vector of integral monic polynomial f: vector of elementary divisors of Z[α]/f(α)Z[α]; components positive and product equals absolute discriminant of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: reduceddiscsmith(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: polinterpolate(xa,ya,{v=x},{&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given data vectors xa and ya of same length, find interpolating polynomial passing through points and evaluate at v; optional e holds error estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: polint(xa,ya,v,&e).

rubrics_metrics.name: polisirreducible(pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether univariate polynomial pol is non-constant and irreducible over smallest base field it appears defined over; returns 1 if irreducible, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gisirreducible(pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollead(x,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Leading coefficient of polynomial or power series x in main variable or v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: pollead(x,v) with omitted v coded -1. Also available: leadingcoeff(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollegendre(n,{v=x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Create nth Legendre polynomial in variable v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: legendre(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrecip(pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal polynomial (coefficients reversed) of polynomial pol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pol must be a polynomial. Library syntax: polrecip(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: polresultant(x,y,{v},{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Resultant of polynomials x and y with exact entries wrt given variable(s); default uses subresultant algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=1 uses determinant of Sylvester matrix (allows inexact coefficients); flag=2 uses Ducos's modified subresultant algorithm (faster for complicated coefficient rings). Library syntax: polresultant0(x,y,v,flag). Alternatives: subres(x,y) (flag=0), resultant2(x,y) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polroots(pol,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute complex roots of polynomial pol returned as column vector with multiplicities; precision per transcendental function conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default algorithm: variant of Schönhage's root-finding by X. Gourdon (guaranteed to converge). flag=1 uses Newton-Raphson variant (faster but not guaranteed). Error messages like 'too many iterations' or 'INTERNAL ERROR' recommend using default. Library syntax: roots(pol,prec) or rootsold(pol,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsmod(pol,p,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Row vector of roots modulo p of polynomial pol; accepts p=4 mainly for 2-adic computations; multiple roots not repeated (unless flag=1 with naive search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p<100 try flag=1 naive search where multiple roots are repeated. Library syntax: rootmod(pol,p) (flag=0) or rootmod2(pol,p) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootspadic(pol,p,r)
rubrics_metrics.description: Row vector of p-adic roots of polynomial pol with p-adic precision r; multiple roots are not repeated; p assumed prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rootpadic(pol,p,r) with r a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: polsturm(pol,{a},{b})
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of real roots of real polynomial pol in ]a,b] using Sturm's algorithm; omitted a or b interpreted as -∞ or +∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: sturmpart(pol,a,b). Use NULL to omit arguments. sturm(pol) is sturmpart(pol,NULL,NULL). Returns a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: polsubcyclo(n,d,{v=x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide polynomial defining a sub-Abelian extension of degree d of cyclotomic field Q(ζ_n) where d|φ(n) and (Z/nZ)* cyclic conditions apply (n = 2,4, pk or 2pk for odd prime p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use galoissubcyclo for the general case. Library syntax: subcyclo(n,d,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsylvestermatrix(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Sylvester matrix for two polynomials x and y, placing coefficients in columns (useful for inexact coefficient cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: sylvestermatrix(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsym(x,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create vector of symmetric powers of roots of polynomial x up to power n, using Newton's formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: polsym(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: poltchebi(n,{v=x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Create nth Chebyshev polynomial in variable v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: tchebi(n,v) where n and v are long integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: polzagier(n,m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create Zagier's polynomial P_{n,m} used in sumalt and sumpos (with flag=1); requires m ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: polzagreel(n,m,prec) for real-coefficient approximations or polzag(n,m) for exact result. Implementation references forthcoming paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: serconvol(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convolution (Hadamard product) of two power series x and y: coefficient-wise product of series coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x = Σ b_k X^k and y = Σ a_k X^k then serconvol(x,y) = Σ (a_k b_k) X^k. Library syntax: convol(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: serlaplace(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laplace transform-like operator on power series with non-negative exponents: map (a_k/k!) X^k to a_k X^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x must be a power series with non-negative exponents. Library syntax: laplace(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: serreverse(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse power series (x^{-1} in the sense of composition inverse, not multiplicative inverse) of x; requires valuation exactly equal to one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: recip(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: subst(x,y,z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace simple variable y by argument z in polynomial-like expression x; substitution rules depend on types and shapes (matrices, vectors, power series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x not genuine polynomial substitution treats scalar components as degree-1 polynomials; substituting non-square matrix is forbidden. If x is power series z must be polynomial, power series or rational function; y must be simple variable name. Library syntax: gsubst(x,v,z) where v is variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: taylor(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor expansion around 0 of x with respect to simple variable y; x may be rational function etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of terms transparent in GP, must be given as second argument in library mode. Library syntax: tayl(x,y,n) where n is desired number of terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: thue(tnf,a,{sol})
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve Thue equation P(x,y)=a in integers using tnf from thueinit(P); optional sol contains solutions of Norm(x)=a modulo units of positive norm in the field defined by P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tnf computed without assuming GRH (flag=1 in thueinit), result is unconditional; otherwise assumes GRH (much faster). Example given: tnf=thueinit(x^13-5); thue(tnf,-4) gives [[1,1]] meaning (x,y)=(1,1) assuming GRH. Library syntax: thue(tnf,a,sol) with omitted sol coded NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: thueinit(P,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize tnf corresponding to polynomial P for use with thue to solve Thue equations P(x,y)=a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, certify results unconditionally (slower); otherwise assume GRH (faster). Library syntax: thueinit(P,flag,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdep(x,k,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given real or complex x, find a polynomial of degree ≤ k having x as approximate root using a variant of LLL (Håstad–Lagarias–Schnorr).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting polynomial is not guaranteed correct or irreducible; check closeness by polynomial evaluation or roots. If precision too low routine may loop. If flag non-zero use standard LLL with flag indicating a precision between 0.5 and 1.0 times decimal digits of x. Library syntax: algdep0(x,k,flag,prec) or algdep(x,k,prec) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: charpoly(A,{v=x},{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic polynomial of matrix A with respect to variable v (determinant of v*I - A); for scalar/polmod returns determinant of map 'multiplication by A'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag selects method: 0 uses trace powers (default), 1 uses Lagrange interpolation (usually slower), 2 uses Hessenberg form (faster for integermod prime or real numbers). Library syntax: charpoly0(A,v,flag). Alternative functions available for specific flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: concat(x,{y})
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenate x and y; non-vector/matrix objects treated as 1D vectors; matrices concatenated horizontally (same number of rows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To concatenate vertically transform vectors to row/column matrices. Empty matrix [;] has compatible row count; empty vectors differ. If y omitted x must be row vector or list; elements concatenated left to right. Examples shown. Library syntax: concat(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: lindep(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector x with real or complex coefficients, find a small integral linear combination among entries (find integer relation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses Hastad–Lagarias–Schnorr LLL variant. flag>0 uses LLL with flag indicating precision parameter. flag<0 returns as soon as one relation found. Library syntax: lindep0(x,flag,prec) or lindep(x,prec) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: listcreate(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an empty list of maximal length n (useless in library mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function primarily for GP interactive use.

rubrics_metrics.name: listinsert(list,x,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert object x at position n in list (type t_LIST), shifting later elements right; can increase effective length up to maximal length set by listcreate (useless in library mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use listput to append or set elements. Only listinsert/listput allow increasing effective length.

rubrics_metrics.name: listkill(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete all elements from list and set effective length to 0 (maximal length unaffected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useless in library mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: listput(list,x,{n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Set n-th element of list to x; if n omitted or greater than current effective length append x. Can increase effective length (useless in library mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To replace element without changing effective length use list[n] = x treating list as vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: listsort(list,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort list (type t_LIST) in place; if flag non-zero suppress repeated coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much faster than vecsort since no copy made. Useless in library mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: matadjoint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjoint (matrix of cofactors) y of square matrix x satisfying x * y = det(x) * Id; x need not be invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: adj(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matcompanion(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Left companion matrix of polynomial x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: assmat(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matdet(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinant of square matrix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses Gauss–Bareiss (default). flag=1 uses classical Gaussian elimination (better for real/integer entries but usually worse for complicated entries). Library syntax: det(x) (flag=0) and det2(x) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: matdetint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer m×n matrix x compute a multiple of determinant of lattice generated by columns if rank m, else return zero; useful to supply modulus to other routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other ways: matdet(qflll(x,4)[2]*x) or matdet(mathnf(x)). Experiment for performance. Library syntax: detint(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matdiagonal(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector x create diagonal matrix with diagonal entries from x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: diagonal(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mateigen(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return eigenvectors of x as columns of a matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: eigen(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathess(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Hessenberg form of square matrix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: hess(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathilbert(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create Hilbert matrix of order x with entries 1/(i+j-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mathilbert(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathnf(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrix x of maximal rank compute upper triangular Hermite normal form (HNF); columns of result form basis of lattice generated by columns of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 naive algorithm. If Z-module is a lattice recommend mathnfmod(x, matdetint(x)). flag=1 uses Batut's algorithm and outputs [H,U] with xU=[0|H]. flag=2 uses Havas's algorithm (unstable in v2.0.19) and outputs [H,U,P]. flag=3 like case1 but outputs [H,U,P]; flag=4 uses Batut with LLL. Library syntax: mathnf0(x,flag). Alias: hnf(x) (flag=0), hnfall(x) (flag=1). For huge sparse matrices hnfspec/hnfadd pair recommended (undocumented).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathnfmod(x,d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute upper triangular HNF of integer matrix x of maximal rank given d a multiple of determinant of lattice spanned by columns; faster than mathnf when d known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: hnf_mod(x,d).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathnfmodid(x,d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Output HNF of x concatenated with d times identity matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: hnf_modid(x,d).

rubrics_metrics.name: matid(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create n × n identity matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: idmat(n). Related functions: gscalmat(x,n) and gscalsmat(x,n) to create scalar times identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: matimage(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a basis for the image of matrix x as columns of a matrix. Matrix may have entries of any type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses standard Gauss pivot; flag=1 uses matsupplement. Library syntax: matimage0(x,flag). Alias: image(x) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: matimagecompl(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return vector of column indices not extracted by matimage; counts complementarity with matimage columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: imagecompl(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matindexrank(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: For matrix x of rank r give two vectors y and z of length r listing rows and columns respectively such that vecextract(x,y,z) is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: indexrank(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matintersect(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two matrices x and y with same number of rows and independent columns, find basis of Q-vector space equal to intersection of column spaces of x and y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See idealintersect for free Z-modules. Library syntax: intersect(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matinverseimage(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a column vector in the inverse image of y by x if one exists, else empty vector; complete inverse image is obtained by adding kernel basis elements (e.g., from matker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: inverseimage(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matisdiagonal(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return true (1) if matrix x is diagonal, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: isdiagonal(x) returning a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: matker(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a basis for the kernel of matrix x as columns of a matrix; matrix may have entries of any type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x known to have integral entries set flag=1. Note ker_mod_p(x,p) is equivalent but much faster and uses less stack; install under GP via install(ker_mod_p,GG). Library syntax: matker0(x,flag). Aliases: ker(x) (flag=0), keri(x) (flag=1), and ker_mod_p(x,p).

rubrics_metrics.name: matkerint(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an LLL-reduced Z-basis for the lattice equal to kernel of integer matrix x (rational entries not permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses modified integer LLL. flag=1 uses matrixqz(x,-2); to avoid LLL at end use matrixqz(matker(x),-2). flag=2 uses another modified LLL requiring independent rows in v2.0.19. Library syntax: matkerint0(x,flag). Alias: kerint(x) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: matmuldiagonal(x,d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiply matrix x by diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are vector d; equivalent to x * matdiagonal(d) but faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matmuldiagonal(x,d).

rubrics_metrics.name: matmultodiagonal(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute product of matrices x and y under assumption result is diagonal; much faster than general multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matmultodiagonal(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matpascal(x,{q})
rubrics_metrics.description: Create as matrix the lower-triangular Pascal triangle of order x+1 (binomial coefficients up to x); if q given compute q-Pascal (q-binomial coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matqpascal(x,q) with q=NULL to omit q. Also available matpascalx.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrank(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return rank of matrix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rank(x) returning a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixqz(x,p)
rubrics_metrics.description: For m×n matrix x with m≥n and rational/integer entries, behavior depends on sign of p: produce integral matrix with same image and GCD properties when p≥0, or compute Zn∩lattice for p=-1, or Zn∩Q-space for p=-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p≥0 assume x maximal rank; p must be prime when non-zero. If p has no small prime factors function may fail with 'impossible inverse modulo' and provide divisor. Library syntax: matrixqz0(x,p).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsize(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return [#rows, #columns] for vector or matrix (row vector rows=1, column vector columns=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matsize(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsnf(X,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return vector of elementary divisors (diagonal of Smith Normal Form) of X; for square X may output full SNF depending on flags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary digits of flag: 1 for complete output [U,V,D] (unimodular U,V such that U X V = D); 2 allows polynomial entries; 4 cleanup (remove elementary divisors equal to 1 and shorten output). If cleanup set and complete output requested returns [U,V,D] cleaned. Library syntax: matsnf0(X,flag). Alias: smith(X) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolve(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve x * u = y for u using Gaussian elimination (x invertible); faster than computing inverse then multiplying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gauss(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolvemod(m,d,y,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integral matrix m, moduli vector d (positive integers) and integral column y, give small integer solution to system of congruences m x ≡ y (mod d) if one exists, else zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: y and/or d can be single integer applied to all components. If flag=1 return all solutions as [x,u] where x is small solution and u columns give basis of homogeneous system. Library syntax: matsolvemod0(m,d,y,flag). Aliases: gaussmodulo(m,d,y) (flag=0) and gaussmodulo2(m,d,y) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsupplement(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming columns of x are linearly independent, find a square invertible matrix whose first columns are columns of x (i.e., supplement columns to a basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If columns not independent an error is issued. Library syntax: suppl(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mattranspose(x) / x~
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose of matrix or vector x (affects only vectors and matrices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gtrans(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfgaussred(q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix q into sum of squares (squared linear forms); output matrix with diagonal entries giving coefficients and off-diagonals bilinear parts so q(x)=Σ a_ii (x_i + Σ_{j>i} a_ij x_j)^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: sqred(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfjacobi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: For real symmetric matrix x return [eigenvalues_vector, orthogonal_matrix_of_eigenvectors] using Jacobi's method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: jacobi(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflll(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply LLL algorithm to columns of (not necessarily square) matrix x (columns must be maximal rank except in some flags); return transformation matrix T such that x·T is LLL-reduced basis of lattice generated by columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag meanings: 0 default does real-number computations (fast but numerically unstable in v2.0.19); 1 assumes integral Gram matrix and computes in integers (accurate, fast); 2 similar to 1 for integer matrices whose columns independent and applies partial reduction before LLL; 3 rational computations only (accurate but extremely slow); 4 integer entries not necessarily maximal rank: returns [kernel_basis, LLL-reduced_image]; 5 like 4 but for polynomial coefficients; 7 older version; 8 like 0 but supports polynomial coefficients; 9 variation on 1 using content. Library syntax: qflll0(x,flag,prec). Aliases: lll(x,prec) (flag=0), lllint(x) (flag=1), lllkerim(x) (flag=4). Note numerical instability warnings for some flags in v2.0.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: qflllgram(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like qflll but input x is Gram matrix (square symmetric real matrix) of lattice vectors; returns transformation matrix T giving coefficients wrt initial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag meanings similar to qflll: 0 numerically unstable in v2.0.19; 1 x has integer entries compute in integers; 4 give kernel and reduced image; 5 same as 4 for generic x; 7 older version. Library syntax: qflllgram0(x,flag,prec). Aliases: lllgram(x,prec) (flag=0), lllgramint(x) (flag=1), lllgramkerim(x) (flag=4).
